newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Mandela opens Southern Africa investment conference.
newsitem.headline: Mandela opens Southern Africa investment conference.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela opens a high-level Southern Africa investment conference on Wednesday as the region grapples with the problem of boosting its sickly competitive position.

Over 600 business leaders and 110 policy-makers are attending the three-day regional Southern African Economic Summit organised by the World Economic Forum (WEF), famous for its annual meeting in Davos, Switzerland.
The conference will focus on trade, infrastructure, privatisation and the competitiveness of the region's industry, which a new report shows to be sadly lacking.

South Africa and Zimbabwe, the area's two leading economies, both scored badly in the WEF's 1997 Global Competitiveness Report, released earlier on Wednesday, ranking 44th and 51st respectively out of a field of 53.

Isaac Takawira, managing director of Barclays Bank Zimbabwe and the Zimbabwean chairman of the conference organising committee, said the key of Southern Africa's future success would lie in integrating the economies of the region.
"We need the economies of scale that a wider regional economy can provide us with," he told reporters ahead of the conference opening.
"Many Southern Africa economies are too small to take on the world economy. But if we group together we will have a much more viable unit," Takawira said.

Leaders of the 12-nation Southern African Development Community (SADC), currently chaired by Mandela, agreed last year to develop a free trade zone over the next eight years, creating a single market of over 130 million people.
Now business wants to see concrete measures to start putting this ideal into practice.

Frederic Sicre, member of the WEF executive board, said Southern Africa would only develop succesfully as a region if governments entered into a partnership with the private sector on a regional and international scale.
SADC consists of Angola, Botswana, Malawi, Mozambique, Mauritius, Lesotho, Namibia, Tanzania, South Africa, Swaziland, Zambia and Zimbabwe.
Mandela is being joined at the conference by Zimabwe's Robert Mugabe and heads of state from other countries in the region.
